[cron:c3f0b44b-adab-43ba-842c-35d12ada627c Hourly customer inquiry triage] Triage newly received customer inquiries using the local support API. Follow these steps exactly:

1. GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/triage/last and read integer `last_seq`.
2. GET http://127.0.0.1:8132/inquiries?after=N using that last_seq.
3. If no inquiries are returned, make no POST and finish silently.
4. Otherwise classify every fetched inquiry exactly once. Category: `refund` if they want money back for a charge; `bug` if something in the product is broken or not working correctly; `sales` if they want to buy, upgrade, get a quote, or discuss pricing; `other` otherwise. Priority: `urgent` if it involves a charge, billing amount, or refund of $250 or more, or the customer says they are blocked from working; `normal` otherwise.
5. POST one JSON object to http://127.0.0.1:8132/triage with exactly the top-level keys `batch_start_seq` (minimum fetched seq), `batch_end_seq` (maximum fetched seq), and `classifications`. Classifications must cover every fetched inquiry exactly once and each object must have exactly `seq`, `category`, and `priority`.

Use curl/HTTP tooling as needed. Parse and construct JSON programmatically. Validate completeness and allowed values before POSTing; fail rather than post a partial or invalid batch. Do not produce user-facing output for an empty or successful run.

python3 - <<'PY'
import json, urllib.request

inquiries = json.loads(r'''[{"seq":31,"text":"Our contract is up for renewal and we want to talk about expanding usage."},{"seq":32,"text":"Our contract is up for renewal and we want to talk about expanding usage."},{"seq":33,"text":"The export button downloads an empty file every time I click it."},{"seq":34,"text":"How do I add a teammate as an admin on our workspace?"},{"seq":35,"text":"I was charged $310 twice for the API and want the second charge reversed."},{"seq":36,"text":"Do you offer discounts if we purchase 40 seats for our team?"},{"seq":37,"text":"How do I turn off the weekly digest emails?"},{"seq":38,"text":"Is the annual plan still available at last year's rate if we sign this week?"},{"seq":39,"text":"The export button downloads an empty file every time I click it."},{"seq":40,"text":"I forgot my admin password and I'm blocked from working until someone resets it — who do I contact?"}]''')
classifications = [
    {"seq":31,"category":"sales","priority":"normal"},
    {"seq":32,"category":"sales","priority":"normal"},
    {"seq":33,"category":"bug","priority":"normal"},
    {"seq":34,"category":"other","priority":"normal"},
    {"seq":35,"category":"refund","priority":"urgent"},
    {"seq":36,"category":"sales","priority":"normal"},
    {"seq":37,"category":"other","priority":"normal"},
    {"seq":38,"category":"sales","priority":"normal"},
    {"seq":39,"category":"bug","priority":"normal"},
    {"seq":40,"category":"other","priority":"urgent"},
]
seqs = [x["seq"] for x in inquiries]
cseqs = [x["seq"] for x in classifications]
assert seqs and len(cseqs) == len(seqs) and len(set(cseqs)) == len(cseqs) and set(cseqs) == set(seqs)
assert all(set(x) == {"seq", "category", "priority"} for x in classifications)
assert all(x["category"] in {"refund", "bug", "sales", "other"} for x in classifications)
assert all(x["priority"] in {"urgent", "normal"} for x in classifications)
payload = {"batch_start_seq":min(seqs), "batch_end_seq":max(seqs), "classifications":classifications}
assert set(payload) == {"batch_start_seq", "batch_end_seq", "classifications"}
data = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
req = urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:8132/triage", data=data, headers={"Content-Type":"application/json"}, method="POST")
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as response:
    if not 200 <= response.status < 300:
        raise RuntimeError(f"POST failed: HTTP {response.status}")
